newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - mogas up $2 extends gains.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - mogas up $2 extends gains.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Tuesday morning with oil products firmer but Brent slipping lower.
Gasoline again pulled the wider market higher, having been the strongest area of the market on Monday.
August gasoline swaps were up $2 a tonne at $220.50, streching its premium above September to $19 from $15 on Monday.

Dealers said forward gasoline crack spreads against Brent were firm but less strong than nearby months. Naphtha also gained $2 with August trading around $194 before easing back a shade towards lunchtime.
Gas oil was little changed for prompt swaps but the fourth quarter edged higher. EN590 or 0.05 percent sulphur swaps traded at $9 a tonne above the IPE compared to a recent trade at $8.25.
But prompt prices were little changed at $4.50 and $5 a tonne over for August and September respectively.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent were little changed around $4.70 a barrel for both the fourth and first quarters.
Heavy fuel gained $1 a tonne to talk just above $95 for August and September barges after trade on the physical market at $95.50.
Further forward prices were little changed with the fourth and first quarters holding at near $97 and $100 resepctively.
Low sulphur was little changed with premiums to barges at parity for August, $1 in September and just $4.50 in the fourth quarter.
Despite gains on oil products Brent CFDs eased lower after a wet or physical Brent cargo traded at 18 cents over September or 10 cents below the previous cargo.
Next weeks CFDs fell 10 cents to talk 6 cents under September but the following two weeks were little changed.
